topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: Prioritizing high-revenue services over navigation safety margins affects link budgets by increasing interference, reducing capacity allocation, and causing latency/jitter. The PHYSICAL mechanism behind this trade-off is rooted in interference analysis, where array factor determines interference patterns. Increased interference leads to reduced capacity allocation, resulting in reduced network reliability and availability. To mitigate these effects, advanced link budgeting techniques and dynamic scheduling algorithms can be employed to optimize resource allocation while maintaining QoS guarantees.
